definition: to discover or get something, especially by searching or by chance.

collocations.example: She hopes to find a job near home.
The editor found a mistake on the first page.

definition: of high quality; very good.

collocations.example: This shop sells clothes of fine quality.
The museum displays many works of fine art.

definition: one of the long thin parts at the end of your hand.

collocations.example: She pointed at the map with her index finger.
He hurt his little finger closing the door.

definition: to complete something or reach the end of it.

collocations.example: I usually finish work at six in the evening.
The team must finish the project by Friday.

definition: the flames, heat, and light produced when something burns.

collocations.example: The dry curtains could easily catch fire.
Firefighters worked quickly to put out the fire.

definition: coming before all others in time, order, or importance.

collocations.example: This is the first time I have flown.
Our team finished in first place this year.

definition: an animal that lives in water and swims using fins.

collocations.example: They went to the lake to catch fish.
The market sells fresh fish every morning.

definition: to be the right size or shape for someone or something.

collocations.example: I can still fit into my old jeans.
The new jacket fits her perfectly.

definition: the number 5.

collocations.example: The company hired five hundred new workers.
The meeting starts at five o'clock sharp.

definition: to repair something that is broken or not working.

collocations.example: The mechanic will fix the car tomorrow morning.
He called a plumber to fix the leak.

definition: smooth and level, without any raised or sloping parts.

collocations.example: Place the box on a flat surface.
The building has a wide flat roof.

definition: one of the levels of a building.

collocations.example: The café is on the ground floor.
Her office is on the top floor.

definition: the colorful part of a plant that produces seeds.

collocations.example: She sells cut flowers at the market.
They planted roses in the flower garden.

definition: to move through the air using wings or in an aircraft.

collocations.example: The birds will fly away when winter comes.
We will fly to London next week.

definition: to do what a rule, instruction, or person tells you.

collocations.example: Please follow the instructions printed on the label.
All staff must follow the safety rules.

definition: the things that people and animals eat.

collocations.example: He eats fast food almost every day.
Doctors advise us to choose healthy food.

definition: the part of the body at the end of the leg.

collocations.example: She injured her left foot while playing soccer.
The child began to stamp her foot angrily.

definition: a game played by two teams who kick a ball.

collocations.example: The boys play football after school every day.
They watched an exciting football match last night.

definition: used to show the person or thing that will get or use something.

collocations.example: I bought a present for her birthday.
There is an important message for you.

definition: a group of people trained and organized for a particular job.

collocations.example: The company expanded its sales force last year.
Half the work force attended the training session.

definition: a large area of land covered with trees.

collocations.example: Many rare animals live in the tropical forest.
A forest fire destroyed hundreds of trees.

definition: to be unable to remember something.

collocations.example: Don't forget about the meeting tomorrow afternoon.
I always forget to lock the back door.

definition: a printed document with spaces for you to write information.

collocations.example: Please complete the application form and sign it.
Fill in the registration form before the class.

definition: lucky; having good things happen to you.

collocations.example: We were fortunate enough to get front seats.
She feels fortunate to have such kind friends.

definition: toward a place or position that is in front.

collocations.example: He took a step forward to greet us.
Please move forward to make room for others.

definition: the number 4.

collocations.example: This region enjoys four distinct seasons each year.
She studied abroad for four years.

definition: costing no money.

collocations.example: They fixed the error for free.
The shop gave every customer a free sample.

definition: to become hard and turn to ice because it is very cold.

collocations.example: The lake will freeze over by December.
The water pipes froze solid during the storm.

definition: recently made, picked, or produced; not old.

collocations.example: The stall offers fresh fruit at low prices.
The bakery sells fresh bread every morning.

definition: the day of the week after Thursday and before Saturday.

collocations.example: The report is due on Friday afternoon.
We will meet again next Friday.

definition: a person you know well and like.

collocations.example: She is my best friend from college.
New students quickly make friends in the club.

definition: a sudden strong feeling of fear.

collocations.example: Many actors suffer from stage fright before shows.
The loud noise gave the children a fright.

definition: used to show the place or time where something starts.

collocations.example: She often works from home on Fridays.
The plan was risky from the start.

definition: the part of a building or thing that faces forward.

collocations.example: Someone is waiting at the front door.
Please leave your key at the front desk.

definition: holding or containing as much as possible.

collocations.example: The train was full of tired passengers.
We started the trip with a full tank.

definition: enjoyment or pleasure.

collocations.example: The children had fun at the beach.
She paints for fun on the weekends.

definition: more; additional.

collocations.example: Please contact us for further information.
The results need further study before publishing.

definition: an activity or sport with rules that people play.

collocations.example: Let's play a game after dinner tonight.
He spends hours playing his favorite video game.

definition: a piece of land next to a house for growing flowers and plants.

collocations.example: The children are playing in the garden.
She waters her flower garden every morning.

definition: a substance like air that is not solid or liquid.

collocations.example: The house is heated by natural gas.
They evacuated the building after a gas leak.

definition: relating to most people or things, not to details.

collocations.example: In general, our customers are very satisfied.
The museum is open to the general public.

definition: calm, kind, and not rough or forceful.

collocations.example: A gentle breeze moved the curtains slowly.
She spoke to the baby in a gentle voice.

definition: to receive or obtain something.

collocations.example: She hopes to get a job after graduation.
Members get a discount on every purchase.

definition: a female child or young woman.

collocations.example: A little girl was feeding the ducks.
They welcomed a healthy baby girl last week.

definition: to hand something to someone for them to keep.

collocations.example: He likes to give a gift on birthdays.
The cashier will give you a receipt.

definition: pleased and happy about something.

collocations.example: I am very glad to meet you today.
She was always glad to help new staff.

definition: a quick short look at something.

collocations.example: You can see the total at a glance.
He took a quick glance at his watch.

definition: a container that you drink from, usually with no handle.

collocations.example: She poured me a glass of water.
He filled each wine glass carefully.

definition: to move or travel to a place.

collocations.example: I want to go home after work.
She goes to work by train every day.

definition: the being that people worship as the creator of the world.

collocations.example: Many people in the village believe in God.
They thanked God for the good harvest.

definition: a valuable, shiny yellow metal used for jewelry and money.

collocations.example: This ring is made of pure gold.
He collects rare gold coins from Europe.

definition: of high quality or an acceptable standard.

collocations.example: Customers expect good quality at a fair price.
She did a good job on the report.

definition: a word you say when you leave someone.

collocations.example: He stopped to say goodbye before leaving.
The children waved goodbye to their teacher.

definition: to officially rule and control a country or area.

collocations.example: It is hard to govern a large country.
The election gave the party the right to govern.

definition: the father of your mother or father.

collocations.example: My grandfather told wonderful stories every evening.
Her maternal grandfather was born in Italy.

definition: a common green plant that covers fields and lawns.

collocations.example: The children ran across the green grass.
He cuts the grass every Saturday morning.

definition: very good; excellent.

collocations.example: The new product was a great success.
Working from home is a great idea.

definition: having the color of grass or leaves.

collocations.example: She wore a dark green coat.
The walls were painted a bright green.

definition: having a color between black and white.

collocations.example: His gray hair made him look older.
The sky turned dark gray before the storm.

definition: the solid surface of the earth.

collocations.example: The children sat on the ground to rest.
The leaves slowly fell to the ground.

definition: a number of people or things that are together.

collocations.example: A group of tourists waited near the gate.
She teaches a small group of students.

definition: to become bigger or increase in amount.

collocations.example: The company has grown quickly this year.
Sales are expected to continue to grow.

definition: to give an answer you are not sure is correct.

collocations.example: Try to guess the answer before checking.
Few people guessed correctly in the contest.

definition: a weapon that fires bullets.

collocations.example: The officer was trained to fire a gun.
He kept a loaded gun in the drawer.

definition: a man.

collocations.example: Our new manager seems like a nice guy.
He acts like a tough guy at work.

definition: the thin thread-like strands that grow on your head.

collocations.example: She tied her long hair in a ponytail.
He prefers short hair in the summer.

definition: one of two equal parts of something.

collocations.example: She cut the apple in half.
The meeting lasted about half an hour.

definition: a large room used for meetings, meals, or events.

collocations.example: The orchestra performed in a famous concert hall.
Students eat lunch in the dining hall.

definition: the part of the body at the end of the arm.

collocations.example: They shook hands after signing the contract.
These letters were written by hand.

definition: the part of an object that you hold to carry or use it.

collocations.example: The door handle was cold to the touch.
The cup had a broken handle.

definition: to attach something at the top so its lower part hangs free.

collocations.example: He wants to hang a picture on the wall.
Please hang your coat on the hook.

definition: to take place, often without being planned.

collocations.example: We must make sure this never happens again.
The accident happened suddenly on the highway.

definition: feeling or showing pleasure.

collocations.example: They sang happy birthday to their grandmother.
The photo showed a happy family together.

definition: difficult to do, understand, or deal with.

collocations.example: The teacher asked a really hard question.
Leaving the company was a hard decision.

definition: almost not; only just.

collocations.example: There was hardly any food left.
She hardly ever arrives late for work.

definition: a covering that you wear on your head.

collocations.example: You should wear a hat in the sun.
She bought a straw hat for the beach.

definition: to dislike someone or something very much.

collocations.example: I hate waiting in long lines.
She hates being late for meetings.

definition: to own, hold, or possess something.

collocations.example: We have a meeting at nine tomorrow morning.
I have a question about the new policy.

definition: used to refer to a man or boy already mentioned.

collocations.example: He said he would arrive before noon.
He works at a bank downtown.

definition: the top part of the body that holds the brain and face.

collocations.example: She shook her head and walked away.
He nodded his head to show agreement.

definition: the condition of your body and how well it is.

collocations.example: Regular exercise is important for good health.
The company offers free health care to staff.

definition: to receive sounds through your ears.

collocations.example: Did you hear a strange sound last night?
She could hear footsteps in the hallway.

definition: the organ in the chest that pumps blood around the body.

collocations.example: Exercise can raise your heart rate quickly.
Smoking increases the risk of heart disease.

definition: the quality of being hot; warmth.

collocations.example: They rested in the shade from the heat of the sun.
The intense heat made it hard to work.

definition: weighing a lot; difficult to lift or move.

collocations.example: She struggled to carry the heavy bag.
The truck carried a very heavy load.

definition: in some religions, a place where bad people are punished after death.

collocations.example: They believed that sinners would go to hell.
The preacher warned about the fires of hell.

definition: a word you say to greet someone.

collocations.example: Stop by the office to say hello sometime.
She greeted each guest with a friendly hello.

definition: to make it easier for someone to do something.

collocations.example: Could you help me carry these boxes?
Several volunteers came to help out today.

definition: in, at, or to this place.

collocations.example: Please come here and look at this.
The manager wants you over here now.

definition: to put something where it cannot be seen or found.

collocations.example: The cat likes to hide from strangers.
She tried to hide the gift away.

definition: greater than usual in amount, level, or quality.

collocations.example: Customers expect high quality from this brand.
The new phone is in high demand.

definition: an area of land higher than the land around it, smaller than a mountain.

collocations.example: The old bus climbed the steep hill slowly.
We walked up the hill to the castle.

definition: all the events that happened in the past.

collocations.example: This was the worst storm in history.
She teaches a class on ancient history.

definition: to strike someone or something with force.

collocations.example: He swung the bat and hit the ball.
The storm hit the coast very hard.

definition: to have or keep something in your hands or arms.

collocations.example: Could you hold the door for me, please?
The child held the rope tightly.

definition: an empty space or opening in something.

collocations.example: There is a hole in my sock.
They dug a hole to plant the tree.

definition: a period of time away from work for rest or travel.

collocations.example: The family went on holiday to Spain.
We are planning a long summer holiday.

definition: the place where you live.

collocations.example: She prefers to relax at home on weekends.
I was too tired, so I went home.

definition: truthful and not likely to lie, cheat, or steal.

collocations.example: Everyone trusts him because he is an honest man.
Please be honest with me about the cost.

definition: great respect given to someone, or something you are proud of.

collocations.example: They held a dinner in honor of the winners.
I have the honor of introducing our speaker.
